paragraphs: Friend, here's the lesson, and it's a big one. Noah, Daniel and Job were the best of the best, and God says their righteousness "could deliver only themselves" (Ezekiel 14:14). Nobody can ride on somebody else's faith. Not a parent's, not a pastor's, not the church lady who brings the good casserole... I mean, the good cookies. Your own walk with God is YOURS.

Now, that can sound heavy, and I think it is a little heavy. But look at it the other way. God isn't being cold here. He's saying every person stands before Him, and He sees every single one. And when the judgment comes on Jerusalem, God still says, "Yet, behold, some survivors will be left in it" (Ezekiel 14:22). Even in a hard passage, He leaves room for people to be brought out.

Then God gives the reason behind it all: "it was not without cause that I have done all these things within it" (Ezekiel 14:23). Nothing He does is random. So, baker, don't coast on anyone else's goodness, and don't throw in the towel when things look dark. Hold on to Him yourself, and trust that He knows exactly what He's doing.
